newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares in downtrend correction.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares in downtrend correction.

text.p: Egyptian share prices dropped slightly on Wednesday in a correction after recent increases, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index fell 0.03 points to close at 233.90 on a volume of 56.21 million pounds ($16.53 million).
"There is a correction after the increases, and that is natural and good," broker Hany el-Beltagy of el-Rashad Securities Brokerage told Reuters.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills was again the market leader with shares worth more than 3.81 million pounds changing hands. The stock rose 0.24 pounds to close at 47.00.
"The share is very good but was offered in small blocks. That's why it declined," a market source said.
Suez Canal Bank was the biggest gainer, rising 3.40 pounds to finish at 52.50 pounds, after 257,000 shares worth 2.6 million pounds were traded.
"The National Bank of Egypt is the most likely seller of the Suez Canal Bank shares," the source said. State-owned banks have started selling off their stakes in other banks.
North Cairo Flour Mills was another active miller jumping 3.00 pounds to close at 115.00 pounds, with shares worth 2.94 million changing hands.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to a new record closing at 369.17 points, its highest level since December 1994, against Tuesday's 368.87.
The index for rarely traded "closed" firms declined to 159.80 points from 159.94
